ig_carousel_topic.topic: What 'units' actually mean (and why win % alone is a lie)
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Your friend went 60-40 last month.
You went 54-46.
He's not up more than you.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
Win percentage is the stat everyone quotes.
It feels clean. It feels like a scoreboard.

The problem: it tells you nothing about how much money moved.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Units measure profit relative to your standard bet size.
1 unit = your base stake, usually 1-2% of your bankroll.

A 54% bettor betting full value beats a 60% bettor chasing bad odds. Every time.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Example:
60% win rate at -150 average odds: roughly -0.9u per 100 bets.
54.5% win rate at -110 average odds: roughly +9u per 100 bets.

The 'worse' win rate is actually the profitable one.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
Win rate is a headline. Units won is the ledger.

We post both every morning, wins and losses included. That's the only number that matters at the end of the year.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Win % is the most quoted and most misleading stat in sports betting. Here's what actually tracks profit over time. 54% can beat 60%. The math is simple once you see it.
